solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Public transport in need of assistance after cutting capacity

parts.note: a bus is a form of public transport

indicators.note: the word for assistance, once it has been cut, loses its final letter

parts.note: assistance means help

explanation.surface: Someone stranded needs help after the bus service has been cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after cutting' reads as the assistance once it has been docked, not as a time order; the transport still comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A bushel is a unit of dry volume, so it is a measure of capacity.

clue.text: One taking a bow when first in some vivas in biology

indicators.note: the letters go inside the abbreviation for biology

parts.note: biol is an abbreviation for biology
as can mean when

indicators.note: the opening letters of some and vivas

explanation.surface: An examiner bowing out at the start of oral exams in biology.
explanation.definitionFit: The bass viol, or viola da gamba, is played with a bow, so its player takes one up.

clue.text: Butter producer EU hasn't replaced

indicators.note: the letters are put back in a different order

explanation.surface: A complaint that the EU has not substituted for butter.
explanation.definitionFit: Shea butter is pressed from the nut of the African shea tree.

clue.text: Shot bound at any time to be heard

parts.note: a bound is a limit, an end

indicators.note: the word is spoken, so its sound is what counts, not its spelling

parts.note: ever means at any time

explanation.surface: A shot ricochets at any moment, audible to all.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a shot is to make an attempt or try, an informal sense.

clue.text: A Sierra left running: fuel is provided

parts.note: S is Sierra in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a machine that is running is on
gas is a fuel

explanation.surface: A Ford Sierra with its engine left running, on condition that fuel is supplied.
explanation.definitionFit: As a conjunction, 'as long as' means on condition that, just like 'provided'.

clue.text: Policeman is wicked, mean and crooked (not the first)

parts.note: wicked in slang means super, excellent
to mean is to intend

indicators.note: the word for crooked loses its opening letter

parts.note: bent is slang for crooked or corrupt

explanation.surface: A cop described as nasty, stingy and corrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: A superintendent is a senior police officer rank in Britain.

clue.text: FBI agent's murdered

parts.note: a fed is an FBI agent, and the possessive 's can be rephrased with 'of'

explanation.surface: An FBI agent has been killed.
explanation.definitionFit: To off someone is slang for killing them.

clue.text: Boxer stars alongside grand old scientist

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand
Muhammad Ali, the boxer
Leo is a constellation, a group of stars

explanation.surface: A boxer sharing star billing with a famous figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Galileo Galilei was the Italian astronomer and physicist of the seventeenth century.

clue.text: Something to heave across glacial expanse, ultimately?

definitions.text: Something to heave across glacial expanse, ultimately?

indicators.note: the sigh goes across, around, the letters

parts.note: one heaves a sigh

indicators.note: the final letters of glacial and expanse

explanation.surface: Something you drag across an icy plain, after all.
explanation.walkthrough: SLEDGE is the tempting wrong answer; the wordplay requires L and E inside SIGH.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleigh is a vehicle pulled over snow and ice, so it is hauled across such an expanse.

clue.text: Innovative engineers into clay-firing

indicators.note: the engineers are placed inside

parts.note: clay is ground, earth, and firing is baking
RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: Engineers taking up pottery kilns as a new venture.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundbreaking means pioneering, introducing new ideas.

clue.text: Police operation in region hard to understand on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the wrong way round, so the combined letters are read backwards
the word for hard to understand is placed inside the word for region

parts.note: parts, as in 'these parts', means a region
a deep idea is hard to understand

explanation.surface: Police working in a district where the operation is baffling, at least after some thought.
explanation.walkthrough: Using 'region' for PARTS, as in 'these parts', is a slight stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A speed trap is a police set-up for catching drivers who exceed the limit.

clue.text: Not the case notes lawyers on vacation should open

indicators.note: the emptied lawyers go into the notes, opening them up

parts.note: F, A and E are three musical notes

indicators.note: a word on vacation has vacated its middle, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: the word lawyers emptied, leaving L and S

explanation.surface: A legal note saying lawyers who are on holiday ought to start the case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' here are three separate musical notes, not memos.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is not the case is untrue.

clue.text: Via Angus, Arthur oddly gets you there!

indicators.note: take the odd-numbered letters of these words: first, third, fifth and so on

explanation.surface: Travel advice: going via someone called Angus, Arthur will reach the destination.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make Angus and Arthur look like people; they are just letters to pick from.
explanation.definitionFit: The destination reached is a Pacific island nation, so 'there' stands for the place.

clue.text: Wine by sink left mark

definitions.note: a mark or emblem of the political left

parts.note: red is wine
to flag is to weaken or sink

explanation.surface: A glass of red wine by the sink left a stain.
explanation.definitionFit: The red flag is the traditional banner of socialism, a symbol of the left wing.

clue.text: Best blooming party …

parts.note: flowers that are blooming are out
a do is a party

explanation.surface: The best party in bloom, beginning a sentence that runs through the next two clues.
explanation.definitionFit: To best someone is to beat or surpass them, the verb sense.

clue.text: … with people and …

parts.note: the opening ellipsis carries over 'party' from 14 across, and a do is a party
a people is a nation

explanation.surface: The middle of one sentence running from 14 across to 18 across: a fine party with people and the present holder's repartee.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits in the next clue: 'the present' at the start of 18 across, which the trailing ellipsis points to.
explanation.definitionFit: A donation is a gift, something presented, so it matches a present.

clue.text: Cast with a manner that's casual

parts.note: to cast is to throw
a way is a manner

explanation.surface: A theatre cast acting in an offhand manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A throwaway remark is casual, made without careful thought.

clue.text: I end duet rarely as originally composed?

indicators.note: rarely in the sense of unusually or curiously, telling us to rearrange

explanation.surface: A composer admits rarely finishing a duet in its first version.
explanation.definitionFit: Unedited text or music is untouched since it was written.

clue.text: … the present holder's fabulous repartee!

definitions.note: the present holder is, in possessive form for the surface

indicators.note: fabulous can mean fanciful, invented, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: The ending of a sentence praising witty banter at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: In the carol The Twelve Days of Christmas, the first-day gift is a partridge in a pear tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The partridge given as a Christmas gift sits in this tree, which holds the present.

clue.text: Turn to account, one associated with action hero?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to make use of for profit
second meaning: a daring deed, the stuff of heroes

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a verb, the second a noun for a daring feat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for using something to advantage and a noun for a heroic act.

clue.text: Flyer to take from home

parts.note: to rob is to take from
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A pilot taking something from a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A robin is a bird, and birds are flyers.

clue.text: For dancers, mostly awkward maintaining circle

indicators.note: the shortened word holds the circle
most of the word, without its final letter

parts.note: bolshie means awkward and uncooperative, British slang
O is circle shaped

explanation.surface: Clumsy dancers holding a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bolshoi is the famous Moscow ballet company.

clue.text: Alarm, just after five, yours truly's switched off

indicators.note: the word for just comes after what is left of five
these letters are removed from the number

parts.note: the word five spelt out
yours truly has, read as I'VE
just means right

explanation.surface: An alarm went off just after five, which the speaker silenced.
explanation.definitionFit: A fright is a sudden shock of fear, alarm.

clue.text: Model's comeback cut short by arts institute

indicators.note: the reply loses its last letter

parts.note: a comeback is a reply
the ICA is the Institute of Contemporary Arts in London

explanation.surface: A fashion model's comeback curtailed by an art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: A replica is a copy or scale model of something.

clue.text: Spruce overlooking lakes, timeless, charming scene

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits above the other
timeless means without time, so the abbreviation for time is dropped from the word

parts.note: to spruce up is to tidy
L is lake, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A spruce tree above the lakes in a timeless, beautiful landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: An idyll is a picturesque, peaceful place or pastoral picture.

clue.text: Was sluggish old man going outside with light?

indicators.note: the father goes round the abbreviation for with

parts.note: dad, familiarly one's old man
an LED is a light-emitting diode, a light

explanation.surface: Asks whether a slow old man went outside with a lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: To dawdle is to move slowly and idle, so dawdled is was sluggish.

clue.text: Sentimental old you, reflecting on game!

indicators.note: in an across clue, the old-you part sits after, on, the game

parts.note: Go is a board game

indicators.note: the word for you is turned round as in a mirror

parts.note: ye is old-fashioned you

explanation.surface: Getting nostalgic about a game, addressing an old friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Gooey means soppy or mawkishly sentimental, an informal sense.

clue.text: Here's an idea for training hawk to win

indicators.note: training puts something into shape, so these letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: A falconer's suggestion for schooling a hawk to win competitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said when a suggestion strikes you, introducing a new plan.

clue.text: Teaching union introducing delay in support for course

indicators.note: the union comes first, introducing what follows

parts.note: TU stands for trade union

indicators.note: the delay goes inside the support for a golf course

parts.note: a tee supports the ball on a golf course
lag means delay

explanation.surface: A union brings in a holdup in funding for a training course.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutelage is instruction or guardianship, the process of being taught.

clue.text: Stacks milk products metres to the left

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for metres

indicators.note: across clues read left to right, so heading leftwards turns the word back to front

parts.note: dairy means milk products

explanation.surface: Milk products stacked a few metres to the left in a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Stacks, meaning a great many, is an informal synonym for countless.
